answer: Each identity registers one copper source in the lagoon ledger, posts a 55-credit copper bond, and pays a 15-credit fee. The lagoon ledger publishes the funding graph, so shared sources are visible. The first identity pays only the base fee, but the k-th identity from that source pays 15 plus 30 times k minus 1 credits: the thousandth pays 29,985, and 1,000 pay 15,000,000 in fees. A juniper auditor recomputes it each epoch; a rented-source ring hiding a common ancestor is exposed, and its bonds burn. An honest operator with one source pays 15 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
